title: Now Is the Month of Maying
description: Thomas Morley's 1595 ballett, for 4 singers (Morley gives the chords' thirds to the tenors, so it needs all four): verse 1 and its "fa la" refrains, each half sung twice, as Morley's own parts with his two tenors joined into one. Light and dancing, every voice with a tune of its own.

credits.arrangement: Thomas Morley (1595), his five voices as four for Stackapella

licence.arrangement: Morley's own parts, public domain; joining the two tenors is original, written for Stackapella: the joined tenor follows the Quintus, taking the Tenor's notes on "Each with", "green-y" and one "la" of the last "Fa la", and A on "play-ing", and sings D on "up-", where the Quintus has F and the Tenor A (F would leap a sixth from "lass", A would move in fifths with the bass). Breaths written in for beginners: "play-ing" is sung as two quarters with a quarter-beat breath after it where Morley holds "play-" for a half note; the tenor's and bass's "la" before the last "Fa la" of each half gives up a beat, their "Fa" coming in half a beat late; each line's last note is shortened. The final chord is held three beats for Morley's longs. Accepted exceptions (singable.py): Morley's own Altus, Bassus and joined tenors in a five-voice ballett: his Altus above his Cantus in the "Fa la" refrains ("la" at beats 23 and 85 to 86.5, and their repeats), its fall of a fourth across the breath to D on "Each", turning back up a third to F on "with", and its leap up a fourth to G on "la" and straight back down to D on "Fa", across his imitative entries; his Bassus's octaves (low G to G on "When mer-", A to A from "grass" to "Fa", G to low G on "la") and its fourths and fifths in "When mer-ry lads", "Each with his bon-ny lass", "up-on the green-y grass" and the "Fa la"s; and the joined tenor's turns in the first "Fa la" (D down to A, then up a third to C; E down to A, then up a fourth to D on "Fa"). Changed in the quality audit (2026-11-13): on "are play-ing" the joined tenor holds A, where it leapt down a fifth to G and back, which left the A7 chord without its root.
licence.source: all five voices from Morley's own part-books, Of Thomas Morley the First Booke of Balletts to Five Voyces (London: Thomas Este, 1595), No. III, Cantus, Altus, Quintus, Tenor and Bassus, read from the microfilm at archive.org/details/bim_early-english-books-1475-1640_the-first-booke-of-balle_morley-thomas-este_1595 (title n0; Cantus n7, Quintus n39, Altus n71, Tenor n103, Bassus n135), every book writing both halves out in full; the soprano is the Cantus, the alto the Altus, the bass the Bassus, every pitch and accidental as printed; spelling modernised ("lasse", "vpon", "grasse"). Checked against E. H. Fellowes, The English Madrigal School, vol. IV (Stainer & Bell, 1913), No. 3, consulted only
